{"id": "d4e9c351-2fd7-43b4-ab25-06064e48d975", "role": "assistant", "content": [{"text": "You're locked in until the term ends. The main things you can still do are use the capacity, avoid a renewal, and ask AWS for billing relief.

**What's fixed**
- You can't delete a Provisioned Throughput bought by model units with a commitment before the term is complete. Yours expires 2027-03-15, about 115 days from now, and billing continues until then whether you use it or not.
- You also can't reduce model units on a committed purchase. After purchase you can only edit the name and tags. You can also change the associated model, but only if it's a custom model, and only to its base model or another custom model from the same base. If `claude-launch-pt` is on a base Claude model, the model can't be changed.

**Options**
1. **Put the capacity to work.** The fee is already sunk, so any traffic you send to the provisioned model ARN avoids on-demand charges you'd otherwise pay. This works if you have other workloads on the same model. Examples are dev and test traffic, evals, batch or backfill jobs, internal tools, or production traffic from other teams. You'd have to point those calls at the provisioned model ARN as the `modelId`. Six invocations in 14 days shows it's nearly idle. The 12 empty days are expected, because CloudWatch returns no datapoints when there were no invocations.
2. **Stop it renewing.** The docs say Provisioned Throughput renews automatically at the end of each term. The documented "cancel auto renew" action is described for token-based Provisioned Throughput. Your resource is model-unit based, so I couldn't confirm from the docs how renewal works for it. Check the full `get-provisioned-model-throughput` output for any renewal setting. If you don't see one, ask AWS Support to confirm before 2027-03-15 that it won't renew, and put a reminder on your calendar a few weeks before that date.
3. **Ask AWS Support or your account manager for relief.** I couldn't find a documented way to cancel early or get a refund. A delayed launch is a reasonable case to raise, but treat any relief as a request that may be declined. Have your account ID, the provisioned model ARN, the purchase date and your usage numbers ready. I can open a support case for you if you want.
4. **Check whether it can be repurposed.** Ask your launch team whether the model can serve another product or team. If it's a custom model, you may also be able to swap it for another custom model from the same base model.

**For future launches**
- Some base models support no-commitment Provisioned Throughput. It bills hourly and you can delete it at any time. That's a safer way to reserve capacity for a date that might slip. The create call omits `commitmentDuration` for this. Check that your model supports it.

I can pull the actual spend on this resource from Cost Explorer so you know what the remaining ~115 days will cost. I can also check whether other on-demand Bedrock usage in the account would fit on this model. Tell me which you'd like.", "type": "text"}], "created_at": null}
